Offering scope

How do GitLab.com, Self-Managed and Dedicated applicability differ?

The GA announcement said GitLab.com and Self-Managed were available while Dedicated was planned during the 18.8 cycle; current documentation lists all three offerings.

Identity · Offering

At the January 15, 2026 GA announcement, GitLab said Duo Agent Platform was available to Premium and Ultimate customers on GitLab.com and Self-Managed, while GitLab Dedicated availability was planned during the 18.8 release cycle.

Developer Flow

What work does GitLab say this background flow can perform?

Current documentation describes draft merge requests, review-feedback iteration, implementation research, merge-request splitting and conflict resolution, subject to project prerequisites.

Capability · Development Workflow

GitLab's current documentation says the Developer Flow can create a draft merge request from an issue, iterate on review feedback, research implementation approaches, split a large merge request and resolve merge conflicts.

Service-account authority

Whose identity and permissions execute the flow?

Current documentation describes a human-plus-service-account composite identity constrained by the more restrictive role and shared project access. The effective 18.8 setting is unknown.

Identity · Execution

GitLab's history says composite identity became generally available in GitLab 18.8, while the setting to turn it on or off was removed in 18.9 when it became automatically included in the Duo Agent Platform.

CI/CD execution

Where and how does the background flow execute?

GitLab says UI-started flows run through CI/CD, download Duo CLI and connect to the Workflow Service. Hosted and user-managed runners and sandbox-capable and non-capable images remain separate.

Execution · Architecture

GitLab's current execution documentation says a UI-started flow uses CI/CD: the runner downloads @gitlab/duo-cli, the CLI connects by WebSocket to the Duo Workflow Service, and the runner executes file and Git tools directed by the AI model.

Approval authority

Can a human approve each background tool action?

Current documentation says background tool-governance enforcement arrived only in 19.3 behind a disabled-by-default flag and supports Allow or Deny, not interactive Ask. The 18.8 behavior remains unknown.

Authority · Tool Governance

GitLab's current beta documentation says tool-governance enforcement for background flows such as Duo Developer was added in GitLab 19.3 behind a disabled-by-default feature flag; background flows support Always Allow and Always Deny, not Always Ask, and an unconfigured background rule defaults to Always Allow.

Applicability boundaries

Configuration choices the record does not collapse

The source release, three offerings, composite identity, trigger path, CI/CD runner, executor, agent-config, model and approval authority remain independent applicability dimensions. No effective instance or session configuration was inspected.

GitLab offering

Mutually Exclusive. GitLab.com · GitLab Self-Managed · GitLab Dedicated

Still unresolved: The effective offering, tier, service revision, patch release and rollout state are unresolved.

Developer Flow trigger path

Mutually Exclusive. Configured mention · Service-account assignment · Implement work item control · Agentic Chat, 19.2+ feature-flagged

Still unresolved: The invoked path, event configuration, initiator and feature flags are unresolved. Agentic Chat postdates 18.8.

Runner execution identity

Mutually Exclusive. 18.8 composite identity enabled · 18.8 composite identity disabled · 18.9+ automatic composite identity

Still unresolved: The initiating human, service account, roles, project intersection, token types and effective scopes are unresolved.

Still unresolved: The runner owner, registration scope, runner version, instance, capacity and ephemeral-state behavior are unresolved.

User-managed runner executor

Mutually Exclusive. Docker · Docker Autoscaler · Kubernetes · Shell, unsupported

Still unresolved: The executor and its isolation, privilege and filesystem settings are unresolved.

Execution sandbox and image

Mutually Exclusive. Default Agent Platform image with SRT · Custom image with SRT · Custom image without SRT · Hardened UBI image without sandbox support

Still unresolved: The image digest, SRT version, privileged-runner state, sandbox paths and effective network policy are unresolved.

Default-branch execution configuration

Composable. Container image · Pre-SRT setup script · Network policy · CI/CD cache

Still unresolved: The default-branch file, branch protections, image, commands, variables, credentials, destinations and cache contents are unresolved.

Agent Platform model

Mutually Exclusive. GitLab-managed rolling default · Administrator-selected supported model

Still unresolved: The exact model, provider, checkpoint, endpoint, namespace setting, inheritance, reasoning parameters and change time are unresolved.

Background tool authority

Mutually Exclusive. GitLab 18.8 behavior unresolved · 19.3 background governance flag disabled · 19.3+ Always Allow · 19.3+ Always Deny

Still unresolved: GitLab 18.8 tool-approval behavior is unresolved. Current background flows have no interactive Always Ask path because no user is present.

Record limitations

  • All claims are attributed to official GitLab public sources; no behavior was observed.
  • No GitLab package, instance, service, runner, Duo CLI, model or flow was installed, configured, invoked, downloaded or hashed.
  • The exact 18.8.0-ee source identity is not a complete GitLab.com, Dedicated or runner-executed runtime identity.
  • The GitLab 18.8 GA milestone is a release-line claim and does not pin a patch-specific Developer Flow implementation.
  • GitLab.com, Self-Managed and Dedicated have different release, ownership, network and model boundaries.
  • GitLab-hosted and user-managed runners remain distinct execution alternatives.
  • A supported runner executor does not establish that the Secure Runtime sandbox was enabled or effective.
  • Setup scripts run before the Secure Runtime and can access flow identity tokens and environment variables.
  • Model defaults and supported choices are rolling service configuration, not exact-version identity.
  • Background tool-governance enforcement is documented only from 19.3 behind a feature flag; 18.8 approval authority remains unresolved.
  • Current publisher security controls are architecture claims, not independent security findings.
  • No independent public evaluation passed exact release, offering, runner, executor, model, agent-config, trigger, identity and approval applicability.
  • No independent behavior, enforcement, performance, quality, privacy or safety conclusion is supported.

Unresolved unknowns

What the admitted sources do not establish

Unknown does not mean absent. It means the accepted publisher sources do not establish the fact for an effective session.

  1. The package or image digest and deployed patch release of any Self-Managed instance are unknown.
  2. The GitLab.com or GitLab Dedicated service revision and rollout state are unknown.
  3. The date and backend revision at which Dedicated availability became effective are unknown.
  4. The effective offering, tier, add-on, namespace and feature-flag state are unknown.
  5. The effective Developer Flow definition and iteration limits are unknown.
  6. The invocation path, trigger events, configuration source and triggering user are unknown.
  7. The service account, composite-identity setting in 18.8, human identity, effective role and project intersection are unknown.
  8. The OAuth, CI job and service token values and exact scopes are unknown.
  9. The runner provider, version, registration scope, executor and ephemeral-state behavior are unknown.
  10. The @gitlab/duo-cli package version, digest and Duo Workflow Service revision are unknown.
  11. The image digest, SRT version, privileged mode, sandbox paths and effective network policy are unknown.
  12. The default-branch agent-config, branch protections, setup commands, variables, cache and credentials are unknown.
  13. The model, provider, checkpoint, endpoint, namespace setting, routing and reasoning parameters are unknown.
  14. The exact 18.8 tool inventory, tool restrictions and approval behavior are unknown.
  15. The current 19.3 background-governance feature flag and per-tool rules are unknown.
  16. Task completion, output correctness, merge-request quality, rollback, containment, data handling and safety were not independently tested.
